question: What is the atomic number of gold, and what is that number multiplied by the atomic number of silver?

subquestions: What is the atomic number of gold (Au)?
What is the atomic number of silver (Ag)?

observations.content:
Summary: Gold is a chemical element with the symbol Au and atomic number 79. This information is consistently provided across all sources, including Auric Jewellery, Wikipedia, Los Alamos National Laboratory, and American Elements. The atomic number signifies the number of protons in the nucleus of a gold atom, which is 79. This number also equals the number of electrons in a neutral gold atom.

[1] Chemical Symbol: Why the Atomic Number is 79 for Gold | Auric Jewellery
    https://www.auricjewellery.com/en-us/blogs/news/what-is-the-chemical-symbol-for-gold-79
    Gold is a chemical element with the symbol Au and atomic number 79. The name is from the Latin: aurum, meaning "shiny dawn". Gold is a dense, soft, shiny solid metal. It is a chemical element of the group of elements known as transition metals. [...] The reason why Chemical Symbol for gold 79 is because if gold was to be placed under a microscope, we would see electrons orbiting around a nucleus that contains 79 protons. Hence why Scientific Chemical Symbol for Gold is Au because its Atomic Number (a number that represents the number of protons in an atom) is 79.

### Why is Gold a Precious Metal? [...] The red-orange metal can be found in nature as nuggets or grains. But it is usually mixed with other metals because pure gold is too soft to work easily. Gold being soft allows you to make gold jewellery by mixing other metals such as silver or copper to make what are called 'gold alloys'.

    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold
    Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79. In its pure form, it is a bright-metallic-yellow, dense, soft, malleable, and ductile metal. Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals. It is one of the least reactive "Reactivity (chemistry)") chemical elements, being the second lowest in the reactivity series, with only platinum ranked as less reactive. answer: Gold (Au) has atomic number **79** [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5], and silver (Ag) has atomic number **47** [S6][S7][S8][S9][S10]. Multiplying them: **79 × 47 = 3713** [S1][S6].
